{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The book's core identification of 'works of the law' as deeds considered in relation to law (whose particular identity is fixed by surrounding context) that cannot purchase justification, the Spirit, covenant standing, or put God in debt best explains the full range of supplied texts without flattening Paul's named distinctions among laws or forcing him into self-contradiction. The strongest counter (NPP-style restriction to Jewish boundary markers) accounts well for the Galatians 2 Antioch setting and circumcision flashpoints but underfits the explicit 'book of the law' and Deuteronomy 27:26 quotation in Galatians 3:10, the knowledge-of-sin and establishment of the law language in Romans 3, and the parallel economic debt language of Romans 4. The book's entry and full proving chapter therefore supply the more economical, text-driven account across every listed occurrence.",
  "book_core_identification": "Paul's phrase for deeds considered in relation to law (not a synonym for obedience and not naming one fixed class of deeds); the surrounding passage may identify God's law, a circumcision-party application, or leave the particular acts unnamed, while what remains constant is the rejected claim that those deeds can purchase justification, produce the Spirit, establish covenant standing, or place God in debt.",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "Distinction between a work (deed) and obedience (relation to a legitimate command); they can coincide without becoming synonyms.",
    "Romans 4 economic picture of works presented for wages/debt rather than faith-versus-obedience as such.",
    "Named-law table (law of God, law of sin, law of the Spirit, law of faith, law of Christ, commandments of God versus men) showing modifiers control referent.",
    "Circumcision itself is not the evil (Paul circumcises Timothy; 1 Cor 7:19 separates the sign from keeping God's commandments); the error is demanding it as purchase price/gate.",
    "Telos of the law as purpose/goal (Christ, love, Spirit-fulfilled right-living) rather than termination; law is established by faith (Rom 3:31).",
    "Not-under-law statements concern dominion/masters and schoolmaster administration, not permission to sin or erasure of the law's definition of right-living; curse is the sentence on the transgressor, not the statute.",
    "Colossians cheirographon is a debt-record, not nomos; Ephesians 2:15 targets the enmity/middle wall; shadows (feasts etc.) are not enemies of their body.",
    "Uniform method of deriving symbols from OT patterns and testing every claim by multiple independent witnesses."
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "New Perspective on Paul / boundary-marker reading: 'works of the law' primarily denotes Jewish covenant identity badges (especially circumcision, food laws, Sabbath/calendar observance) that mark ethnic Israel off from Gentiles; Paul's polemic targets the requirement that Gentiles adopt those markers for full covenant membership rather than human effort, moral performance, or Mosaic law-keeping as such.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Primarily Jewish ethnic/covenant boundary practices (circumcision, food laws, calendar/Sabbath) rather than the Mosaic Torah as a whole, general moral effort, or any deeds whose claim to purchase standing is rejected.",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "SAME_CORE_NARROWER",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter denies that the phrase can, in any occurrence, refer to deeds under God's law itself (or leave the acts unnamed) provided only that the rejected claim is purchase of justification/Spirit/standing; it insists the referent is restricted to ethnic identity markers.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Galatians 2:11-16 introduces the phrase precisely in the Antioch table-fellowship dispute driven by 'them which were of the circumcision' and the compulsion that Gentiles 'live as do the Jews.'",
    "Galatians 5:2-6 and 6:12-15 make circumcision the explicit flashpoint for justification-by-law claims and boasting.",
    "Romans 3:29-30 immediately after 3:28 asks whether God is God of Jews only, linking the phrase to Jew-Gentile unity.",
    "Acts 15 circumcision controversy and 4QMMT ('some of the works of the Torah') supply contemporary Second-Temple parallels for a technical boundary-marker sense.",
    "Romans 4:9-12 and Colossians 2:16 are often read as further evidence that the contested practices are precisely the markers of Jewish identity."
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Handles every listed occurrence with one consistent rule (context identifies the work; the phrase denies the purchase-price claim) rather than forcing a single fixed class of deeds onto all texts.",
    "Accounts for explicit identification with God's law and the Deuteronomic curse quotation in Galatians 3:10 without special pleading.",
    "Preserves Romans 3:20 (knowledge of sin), 3:31 (we establish the law), and the holy/spiritual/delight language of Romans 7 without contradiction.",
    "Integrates the debt/wages picture of Romans 4 and the parallel 'not of works' statements (Eph 2, Titus 3, 2 Tim 1) that are not limited to ethnic badges.",
    "Explains why Paul can circumcise Timothy, keep Pentecost, and demonstrate law-keeping (Acts 16, 20, 21) while still rejecting works-of-the-law justification claims.",
    "Avoids collapsing Paul's carefully named laws into one bucket, thereby preventing the self-contradictions that arise under both pure legalism and pure boundary-marker reductions."
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Gives a historically and rhetorically precise account of the Galatians 2 Antioch crisis and the circumcision party's demands.",
    "Supplies a Second-Temple parallel (4QMMT) that matches the Greek phrasing.",
    "Tightly links the phrase to the Jew-Gentile inclusion theme that dominates Galatians and Romans 3-4.",
    "Avoids the anachronistic 'legalism vs. grace' frame sometimes read into Second-Temple Judaism."
  ],
  "evidence_book_core_cannot_explain": [],
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "decisive_sources": [
    "Galatians 3:10 (explicit 'book of the law' + Deut 27:26 curse on failure to do all that is written)",
    "Romans 3:20, 28, 31 (law gives knowledge of sin; justification without works of the law; we establish the law)",
    "Romans 4:1-8 (works as wages/debt vs. faith counted as righteousness)",
    "Galatians 2:16 in its 2:11-14 setting (circumcision-party application) together with 1 Cor 7:19 and Acts 16:3 (sign vs. commandments of God)",
    "Galatians 3:2, 5 (Spirit by hearing of faith vs. works of the law; acts left unnamed)",
    "Romans 9:32 KJV/TR and the named-law distinctions of Romans 7-8",
    "Full proving chapter's classification table and telos/schoolmaster/curse distinctions"
  ],
  "unresolved_objections": [
    "The precise semantic weight of 4QMMT remains debated and could still color Galatians 2 even if it does not control every occurrence.",
    "Whether every 'works of the law' instance in Galatians 3:2,5 must be read as circumcision-party application or can remain genuinely ambiguous is underdetermined by the letter alone.",
    "Some secondary elaborations (e.g., exact scope of Colossians 2 shadows or Ephesians 2 ordinances) invite further debate without overturning the core purchase-price denial."
  ],
  "confidence": "high"
}
